name: WorkMeetingSprintPlanning_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Sprint planning meeting. Felix, Zara, Omar, Amara and Kenji. Hybrid. Amara is advocating for a feature engineering thinks is under-scoped. A scope disagreement plays out constructively.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Conference room, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a sprint planning meeting. Felix facilitates. Amara wants to include a feature that Omar and Zara think needs more scoping. Kenji has a design dependency. Story points get estimated with friction. Sigma is asked for a date or previous sprint velocity.

variations.context: Sprint planning, scope debate, 5-person hybrid team

setting.mood: Focused with underlying tension over scope.
setting.relationship_dynamic: PM vs engineering — recurring negotiation, not personal.
setting.background: Sprint starts Monday. They need to commit today.

scenario_template.topic: Felix opens. Amara gives overview of what she wants in the sprint.
scenario_template.note: Felix has the sprint goal. Amara has her list. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Engineering pushes back on one story — not enough scoping, too many unknowns.
scenario_template.note: Zara and Omar are aligned. Amara makes the business case. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Kenji raises a design dependency nobody had flagged.
scenario_template.note: Not a blocker but it changes the estimate. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Felix or Omar asks Sigma for a date or velocity figure.
scenario_template.note: Brief lookup. Informs estimation. No assistant present. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Points agreed, sprint committed, one item deferred.
scenario_template.note: Not everyone fully happy. Sprint starts Monday. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

user1.name: Felix
user1.role: Facilitates. Pushes toward decision. Keeps engineering and PM aligned.

user2.name: Zara
user2.role: Will not commit to unclear scope. Evidence-based pushback.

user3.name: Omar
user3.role: Aligned with Zara. More diplomatic about it.

user4.name: Amara
user4.role: Has the business case. Will negotiate but has a line.

user5.name: Kenji
user5.role: Design dependency is real. Not trying to derail.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
